# Cratis

> Cratis helps teams build business systems they can explain and change: preserve event history, keep backend and frontend contracts in step, and make expected behavior explicit. Cratis Build brings together MIT-licensed tools, including Chronicle for event sourcing and Arc for CQRS with or without event sourcing. Cratis Studio is an optional paid modeling workspace built on Chronicle, with open sign-up, a 14-day free trial and per-seat pricing. Cratis Direct is the control plane for agentic engineering; access opens in stages. Cratis Assurance provides paid expertise, support, reviews and workshops.

## Cratis

- [Home](https://cratis.no/): Company and lifecycle overview.
- [The Cratis stack](https://cratis.no/stack/): How Chronicle, Arc and the tools around them fit together.
- [The cast](https://cratis.no/stack/the-cast/): How Cratis names its products and capabilities.
- [Why Cratis](https://cratis.no/why-cratis/): When Cratis fits, and when it is the wrong choice.
- [Cratis Studio](https://cratis.no/studio/): Agree on business behavior together. Optional paid product built on Chronicle; sign-up is open with a 14-day free trial and per-seat pricing at https://cratis.studio.
- [Cratis Direct](https://cratis.direct): The control plane for agentic engineering. Journeys, gates and recorded evidence keep agent work accountable. GitHub-first, bring your own model provider, event-sourced on Chronicle, and used for Cratis's own engineering. Access opens in stages.
- [Cratis Assurance](https://cratis.no/support/): Support, reviews, first slices and workshops.
- [Trust](https://cratis.no/trust/): Open-source scope, security, continuity and current practices.
- [Cratis AI and Direct](https://cratis.no/ai/): Framework guidance for assistants, and journeys, gates and evidence for governing agentic engineering. Neither replaces engineering review.
- [About](https://cratis.no/about/): The team and the thinking behind Cratis.

## Documentation

- [Cratis documentation](https://www.cratis.io/): Product documentation, tutorials and API reference.
- [Adopt Cratis in an existing system](https://www.cratis.io/adopting-cratis/): Choose a bounded starting point; keep current-state storage where history is not needed.
- [Chronicle](https://www.cratis.io/chronicle/): Preserve business events and derive read models from recorded history.
- [Arc](https://www.cratis.io/arc/): Typed commands, queries and generated TypeScript proxies, with or without event sourcing.
- [Screenplay](https://www.cratis.io/screenplay/): Describe business behavior in a portable .play model.
- [Stage](https://www.cratis.io/stage/): Compile models, verify supported specifications and explore supported behavior in disposable sandboxes, not production hosting.
- [Cratis Choreography](https://www.cratis.io/choreography/): Durable jobs, workflows, state machines and workers on Orleans.
- [Capability map](https://www.cratis.io/cratis-stack/#capability-map): Product responsibilities, licenses and service terms across the stack.
- [Support matrix](https://www.cratis.io/compatibility/#support-matrix): Storage, client languages and hosting, including the Go client's lack of observers and projections; not a guarantee of feature parity.
- [Spec-driven development](https://www.cratis.io/spec-driven-development/): Model contracts, executable specifications and acceptance scenarios.
- [Event sourcing and GDPR](https://www.cratis.io/concepts/event-sourcing-gdpr/): Crypto-shredding and the erasure responsibilities that remain.
- [First application](https://www.cratis.io/templates/getting-started/): Scaffold and run a local full-stack application.
- [Cratis Studio](https://cratis.studio): The hosted paid Studio product; sign-up is open with a 14-day free trial and per-seat pricing.

## Writing

- [Writing](https://cratis.no/writing/): Essays on building systems that can account for themselves.
- [Give it a vague codebase and it produces vague code, faster](https://cratis.no/writing/vague-codebase-vague-code/): On AI assistants and the structure they work inside.
- [Cratis blog](https://blog.cratis.io): Engineering posts from the Cratis team.
